name: Marcassa

the bumbling hero prince, little cinders, who found the bird and wed Marcassa

sources: Luzel, François-Marie. Celtic Folk-Tales from Amorica. Translated by Derek Bryce. Dyfed, Wales: Llanerch Enterprises, 1985. Page 84.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Marcassa was a Breton heroine. A traditional Breton folktale tells of her beautiful distant castle, where a magical bird roosted. The bird held the cure for the mysterious illness of the land's ruler. The hero prince Luduenn, meaning little cinders, set off to find the bird and speed the king's recovery. His two older brothers had gone forth and never returned. Luduenn found them living wild in a distant city. They stole his little money and turned him out. He found Marcassa's palace and the bird caged in gold. The kiss he took from the sleeping princess made her pregnant. When her son was a year old, she went in search of the father and found the evil brothers. Marcassa told the king what she had learned, and the king had the dissolute boys killed. He installed Marcassa and Luduenn as king and queen. The story shares much with the Scottish folktale of Brian and Dér Gréine.

okr.objective: Document Marcassa, the Breton heroine of the folktale of the magical bird.
